dedupe_keys.name: open telecom data good practice wiki terrestrial fibre network maps

description: This wiki page collects examples of good practice in publishing terrestrial fibre-optic network data. Contents: short entries on Zayo (United States; fibre routes and points of presence map), OpenNet Georgia (state-funded backbone with an interactive map and downloadable KML and Excel data), ARCEP France (FTTH deployment map down to household level with the underlying open data), Dark Fibre Africa (an online South African map served by an ArcGIS public API), Open Eir in Ireland (detailed rollout map), Liquid Telecom (map without points of presence or exact routes, described as limited), Telefónica Spain (duct and register database open to registered operators) and BCN Nigeria (maps of existing and planned FTTH). Producer: the Open Telecom Data community wiki. Coverage: the operators named, across Europe, Africa, the United States and the Caucasus. Access: a public wiki page linking to each operator's own map or data. Licence and cost: free to read; each linked dataset has its own terms. Caveats: the entries are qualitative descriptions and links, not the data, and some links or access routes may have changed. Simulation uses: it points to open fibre route and point-of-presence data for network topology, resilience and hazard-exposure models. Related record: ARCEP FTTH deployments (data-arcep-ftth-deployments-cartefibre).
